items.headline: I built a tool that evaluates RAG responses and detects hallucinations
items.summary: When debugging RAG systems, it’s hard to know whether the model hallucinated or retrieval failed.  So I built EvalKit.   Input: • question • retrieved context • model response   Output: • supported claims • hallucination detection • answerability classification • root cause   Curious if this helps others building RAG systems. https://evalkit.srivsr.com    submitted by    /u/Chemical-Raise5933   [link]   [comments]

items.headline: (Llama.cpp) In case people are struggling with prompt processing on larger models like Qwen 27B, here's what helped me out
items.summary: TLDR: I put the --ubatch-size to my GPU's L3 cache is (in MB).  I was playing around with that value, and I had a hard time finding what exactly it did, or rather, I couldn't really understand it from most of the sources, and asking AI chats for help yielded very mixed results. My GPU is 9070xt, and when I put it to --ubatch-size 64 (as the GPU has 64MB of L3 cache) my prompt processing jumped in speed where it was actually usable for Claude code invocation.
